arxiv-2108-11018.title: A Scaling Law for Syn2real Transfer: How Much Is Your Pre-training Effective?
arxiv-2108-11018.creator: Hiroaki Mikami, Kenji Fukumizu, Shogo Murai, Shuji Suzuki, Yuta Kikuchi, Taiji Suzuki, Shin-ichi Maeda, Kohei Hayashi
arxiv-2108-11018.description: Abstract Synthetic-to-real transfer learning is a framework in which a synthetically generated dataset is used to pre-train a model to improve its performance on real vision tasks. The most significant advantage of using synthetic images is that the ground-truth labels are automatically available, enabling unlimited expansion of the data size without human cost.

arxiv-2110-06321.title: Controller-based Energy-Aware Wireless Sensor Network Routing using Quantum Algorithms
arxiv-2110-06321.creator: Jie Chen, Prasanna Date, Nicholas Chancellor, Mohammed Atiquzzaman, Cormac Sreenan
arxiv-2110-06321.description: Abstract Energy efficient routing in wireless sensor networks has attracted attention from researchers in both academia and industry, most recently motivated by the opportunity to use SDN (software defined network)-inspired approaches. These problems are NP-hard, with algorithms needing computation time which scales faster than polynomial in the problem size.

arxiv-2208-07779.title: Steps to Knowledge Graphs Quality Assessment
arxiv-2208-07779.creator: Elwin Huaman
arxiv-2208-07779.description: Abstract Knowledge Graphs (KGs) have been popularized during the last decade, for instance, they are used widely in the context of the web. In 2012 Google has presented the Google’s Knowledge Graph that is used to improve their web search services.

arxiv-2307-12447.title: Random Kronig-Penney-type potentials for ultracold atoms using dark states
arxiv-2307-12447.creator: Mateusz Łącki, Jakub Zakrzewski
arxiv-2307-12447.description: Abstract A construction of a quasi-random potential for cold atoms using dark states emerging in Λ \Lambda level configuration is proposed. Speckle laser fields are used as a source of randomness. Anderson localisation in such potentials is studied and compared with the known results for the speckle potential itself.

arxiv-2309-06996.title: Dynamics Reflects Quantum Phase Transition of Rabi Model
arxiv-2309-06996.creator: M. Li, Y. N. Wang, Z. Y. Song, Y. M. Zhao, X. L. Z ​ h ​ a ​ o ∗ Zhao^{*}, H. Y. M ​ a † Ma^{{\dagger}}
arxiv-2309-06996.description: Abstract As the simplest and most fundamental model describing the interaction between light and matter, a breakdown in the rotating wave approximation of the Rabi model leads to phase transition versus coupling strength when the frequency of the qubit greatly surpasses that of the oscillator.

arxiv-2405-03901.description: Abstract . The progression to “Pervasive Augmented Reality” envisions easy access to multimodal information continuously. However, in many everyday scenarios, users are occupied physically, cognitively or socially. This may increase the friction to act upon the multimodal information that users encounter in the world.

arxiv-2407-00340.title: The Echoes of the ’I’: Tracing Identity with Demographically Enhanced Word Embeddings
arxiv-2407-00340.creator: Ivan Smirnov
arxiv-2407-00340.description: Abstract Identity is one of the most commonly studied constructs in social science. However, despite extensive theoretical work on identity, there remains a need for additional empirical data to validate and refine existing theories. This paper introduces a novel approach to studying identity by enhancing word embeddings with socio-demographic information.

arxiv-2409-12378.title: Star cluster formation from turbulent clumps. IV. Protoplanetary disc evolution
arxiv-2409-12378.creator: Aayush Gautam, Juan P. Farias, Jonathan C. Tan
arxiv-2409-12378.description: Abstract Most stars are born in the crowded environments of gradually forming star clusters. Dynamical interactions between close-passing stars and the evolving UV radiation fields from proximate massive stars are expected to sculpt the protoplanetary discs in these clusters, potentially contributing to the diversity of planetary systems that we observe.

arxiv-2503-13477.title: Periodontal Bone Loss Analysis via Keypoint Detection With Heuristic Post-Processing
arxiv-2503-13477.creator: Ryan Banks, Vishal Thengane, María Eugenia Guerrero, Nelly Maria García-Madueño, Yunpeng Li, Hongying Tang, Akhilanand Chaurasia
arxiv-2503-13477.description: Abstract Objectives: This study proposes a deep learning framework and annotation methodology for the automatic detection of periodontal bone loss landmarks, associated conditions, and staging. Methods: 192 192 periapical radiographs were collected and annotated with a stage agnostic methodology, labelling clinically relevant landmarks regardless of disease presence or extent.

arxiv-2510-02480.title: Safe and Efficient In-Context Learning via Risk Control
arxiv-2510-02480.creator: Andrea Wynn, Metod Jazbec, Charith Peris, Rinat Khaziev, Anqi Liu, Daniel Khashabi, Eric Nalisnick
arxiv-2510-02480.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate a remarkable ability to learn new tasks from a few in-context examples. However, this flexibility introduces safety concerns: LLMs can be influenced by incorrect or malicious demonstrations – for example, if an adversary tampers with or injects harmful examples without a human supervisor noticing.

arxiv-2510-04136.title: MoME: Mixture of Matryoshka Experts for Audio-Visual Speech Recognition
arxiv-2510-04136.creator: Umberto Cappellazzo, Minsu Kim, Pingchuan Ma, Honglie Chen, Xubo Liu, Stavros Petridis, Maja Pantic
arxiv-2510-04136.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Umberto Cappellazzo, Minsu Kim, Pingchuan Ma, Honglie Chen, Xubo Liu, Stavros Petridis, Maja Pantic. Large language models (LLMs) have recently shown strong potential in audio-visual speech recognition (AVSR), but their high computational demands and sensitivity to token granularity limit their practicality in resource-constrained settings. Token compression methods can reduce inference cost, but they require fixing a compression rate in advance and produce a single fixed-length output, offering no flexibility to balance information density and efficiency at inference time.

pmc-10604716.creator: Abdelrahman M Elhusseiny, Giuliano Scarcelli, Osamah J Saeedi, Dimitrios Karamichos
pmc-10604716.description: Over the last two decades, there has been growing interest in assessing corneal biomechanics in different diseases, such as keratoconus, glaucoma, and corneal disorders. pmc-12589709.title: Soil phosphate availability drives shifts between arbuscular mycorrhizal and ectomycorrhizal fungi in the dual mycorrhizal plant Quercus serrata
pmc-12589709.creator: Tatsuhiro Ezawa, Chika Mizukami, Anjar Cahyaningtyas, Mana Mukai, Kanehiro Kitayama

pmc-13261307.description: Formate dehydrogenase (FDH) catalyzes the reversible formate oxidation using NAD+ to yield carbon dioxide and NADH.
